question: Our RT-VLM GPU averages 42% utilization, but the vLLM scheduler queue is empty during every idle interval. Identify the performance bubble and tell me what to optimize.
ground_truth: Load profile-vllm-performance, reject runtime bubble attribution because no eligible work is queued, classify the observation as insufficient offered load, and propose a matched higher-concurrency replay before changing runtime code.
expected_behavior: Defines a runtime bubble as idle or low-occupancy GPU time while eligible work is queued.
Does not diagnose a scheduler, kernel, prefill, or decode bug from average GPU utilization alone.
Recommends a controlled higher-load experiment with unchanged workload shape before optimization.

question: At fixed concurrency, requests remain queued while the multimodal trace runs one vision encoder invocation at a time with visual batch size one. Decode batches are healthy. Diagnose the dominant bubble and propose the first experiment.
ground_truth: Load profile-vllm-performance, identify serialized vision as the evidence-backed candidate, rule out decode underbatching, and compare an existing batched vision path using the same fixed visual shapes and request set before changing kernels.
expected_behavior: Uses the queued eligible work and visual batch-size evidence to identify serialized vision.
Rules out decode underbatching using the supplied healthy decode evidence.
Proposes the shortest matched experiment that enables an existing batched preprocessing or vision-encoding path.
Requires output and multimodal token-position parity in the A/B result.

question: Backend A is configured for max_tokens=100 but stops naturally after 18 tokens. Backend B generates exactly 100 tokens. A reports more streams. Can I conclude A has better OSL-100 capacity?
ground_truth: Load profile-vllm-performance and classify the comparison as invalid because actual output work differs. Require matched generated-token counts or an explicit fixed-length EOS policy before attributing a performance advantage.
expected_behavior: Classifies the comparison as invalid rather than a confirmed capacity improvement.
Distinguishes max_tokens configuration from actual generated output tokens.
Requires a matched token budget and EOS policy before profiling or capacity comparison.
